front.title: PQ/T Hybrid Composite Signatures for JOSE and COSE

abstract.t: This document describes JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) serializations for Post- Quantum Traditional (PQ/T) hybrid composite signatures. The composite algorithms described combine the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) as the post-quantum component and either the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) or the Edwards-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA) as the traditional component.

front.title: Composite Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) for use in X.509 Public Key Infrastructure

abstract.t: This document defines combinations of US NIST Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) in hybrid with traditional algorithms RSASSA-PKCS1-v1.5, RSASSA-PSS, ECDSA, Ed25519, and Ed448. These combinations are tailored to meet regulatory guidelines in certain regions. Composite ML-DSA is applicable in applications that use X.509 or PKIX data structures that accept ML-DSA, but where the operator wants extra protection against breaks or catastrophic bugs in ML-DSA, and where existential unforgeability (EUF-CMA) level security is acceptable.

front.title: Certificate Transparency

abstract.t: This document describes an experimental protocol for publicly logging the existence of Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates as they are issued or observed, in a manner that allows anyone to audit certificate authority (CA) activity and notice the issuance of suspect certificates as well as to audit the certificate logs themselves. The intent is that eventually clients would refuse to honor certificates that do not appear in a log, effectively forcing CAs to add all issued certificates to the logs.
Logs are network services that implement the protocol operations for submissions and queries that are defined in this document.

front.title: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0

abstract.t: This document describes version 2.0 of the Certificate Transparency (CT) protocol for publicly logging the existence of Transport Layer Security (TLS) server certificates as they are issued or observed, in a manner that allows anyone to audit certification authority (CA) activity and notice the issuance of suspect certificates as well as to audit the certificate logs themselves. The intent is that eventually clients would refuse to honor certificates that do not appear in a log, effectively forcing CAs to add all issued certificates to the logs.
This document obsoletes RFC 6962. It also specifies a new TLS extension that is used to send various CT log artifacts.
Logs are network services that implement the protocol operations for submissions and queries that are defined in this document.

front.title: Improving Awareness of Running Code: The Implementation Status Section

abstract.t: This document describes a simple process that allows authors of Internet-Drafts to record the status of known implementations by including an Implementation Status section. This will allow reviewers and working groups to assign due consideration to documents that have the benefit of running code, which may serve as evidence of valuable experimentation and feedback that have made the implemented protocols more mature.

This process is not mandatory. Authors of Internet-Drafts are encouraged to consider using the process for their documents, and working groups are invited to think about applying the process to all of their protocol specifications. This document obsoletes RFC 6982, advancing it to a Best Current Practice.

front.title: Guidelines for Writing RFC Text on Security Considerations

abstract.t: All RFCs are required to have a Security Considerations section. Historically, such sections have been relatively weak. This document provides guidelines to RFC authors on how to write a good Security Considerations section. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Privacy Considerations for Internet Protocols

abstract.t: This document offers guidance for developing privacy considerations for inclusion in protocol specifications. It aims to make designers, implementers, and users of Internet protocols aware of privacy-related design choices. It suggests that whether any individual RFC warrants a specific privacy considerations section will depend on the document's content.

front.title: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS)

abstract.t: Cryptographic operations like hashing and signing need the data to be expressed in an invariant format so that the operations are reliably repeatable. One way to address this is to create a canonical representation of the data. Canonicalization also permits data to be exchanged in its original form on the "wire" while cryptographic operations performed on the canonicalized counterpart of the data in the producer and consumer endpoints generate consistent results.

This document describes the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS). This specification defines how to create a canonical representation of JSON data by building on the strict serialization methods for JSON primitives defined by ECMAScript, constraining JSON data to the Internet JSON (I-JSON) subset, and by using deterministic property sorting.

front.title: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts

abstract.t: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts prove properties of a Verifiable Data Structure (VDS) to a verifier. VDSs and associated Proof Types enable security properties, such as minimal disclosure, transparency, and non-equivocation. Transparency helps maintain trust over time and has been applied to certificates, end-to-end encrypted messaging systems, and supply chain security. This specification enables concise transparency-oriented systems by building on Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) and COSE. The extensibility of the approach is demonstrated by providing CBOR encodings for Merkle inclusion and consistency proofs.

front.title: ML-DSA for JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE)

abstract.t: This document specifies JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) serializations for the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard (ML-DSA), a Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) digital signature scheme defined in US NIST FIPS 204.

front.title: Selective Disclosure CBOR Web Tokens (SD-CWT)

abstract.t: This specification describes a data minimization technique for use with CBOR Web Tokens (CWTs). The approach is inspired by the Selective Disclosure JSON Web Token (SD-JWT), with changes to align with CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) and CWTs.

Its leaf is the statement's ; deterministic COSE_Sign1 encoding with an empty unprotected header, ; hashed SHA-256(0x00 || leaf) (RFC 9162). Read by the host's rule ; only; the statement's schema never reads it. ; protected, unprotected, payload, signature ceg-receipt = #6.18([bstr, { 396: { * int => [+ bstr] }, * int => any }, bstr / nil, bstr])
statement-protected = { ; alg: the composite ML-DSA-65-Ed25519; private-use until IANA ; assigns, the construction exactly the draft's 1: composite-alg, ; cty: the constant, with no parameters 3: row-cty, ; kid: the RFC 9679 thumbprint of the signer's AKP composite key ; (below) 4: kid, ; RFC 9597: iss and sub as RFC 9943 requires 15: cwt-claims, ; typ (RFC 9596): a row's typ is fixed 16: "ceg-row/2", ; the row's type, one of the five; the row id reads it -70001: row-type, ; the row's family id, never a leaf; the row id reads it -70002: family-id, }
composite-alg = -70100 kid = bstr .size 32 ; the RFC 9679 SHA-256 thumbprint
; cty is one constant with no parameters; a verifier refuses any ; other. The type and the family ride their own labels, -70001 and ; -70002, required on a row and refused on any other object. `family` ; is a family id, never a leaf: the registry prefix with each {name} ; written .name and each * written . (so ; `evidence:.suite:.kind:.cell:.prefix`, `accord:.`). row-cty = "application/vnd.ciris.row+cbor" row-type = "scores" / "delegates_to" / "supersedes" / "withdraws" / "recants" family-id = tstr .regexp "[a-z0-9_.][a-z0-9_.-]*(:[a-z0-9_.][a-z0-9_.-]*)*"
cwt-claims = { ; iss: the signer's stable identity reference (its genesis key's ; thumbprint URI), never the rotating kid; under a room key, iss is ; the voice, the identity reference of the voice's first room key, ; never its person's 1: identity-ref, ; sub: what the row is about; a key subject is an identity-ref 2: tstr, ; iat: floor(asserted_at / 1000), seconds, derived; a verifier ; refuses disagreement 6: uint, ; nbf: floor(valid_from / 1000) where the row has one ? 5: uint, ; exp: floor(valid_until / 1000) where the row has one ? 4: uint, -70003: 2, ; edition: the constant 2 }
; One spelling for every identity reference: iss, author, a key ; subject in sub or subject_key_ids, and every role party. The COSE ; Key Thumbprint URI of RFC 9679 Section 5.7 with the hash name ; sha-256 and the 32-byte thumbprint in unpadded base64url (43 ; characters, the last carrying zero trailing bits). identity-ref = tstr .regexp ("urn:ietf:params:oauth:ckt:sha-256:[A-Za-z0-9_-]{42}[AEIMQUY" .cat "cgkosw048]")
; No float, no null, no undefined, no tag anywhere a family member ; can reach. The exceptions are SD-CWT's redaction (simple(59) as a ; map key, tag 60 for an array element) and a body's tag-4 decimal. ceg-value = int / tstr / bstr / bool / body-decimal / [* (ceg-value / redacted-element)] / { ? redacted_claim_keys => [+ bstr .size 32], * (tstr / int) => ceg-value } ; A non-integral number in a free-form body (CC 2.6.1.2): tag 4, ; [exponent, mantissa], in CBOR's integer range. Normalisation (a ; mantissa not divisible by 10) is checked in prose; an integral ; number is a plain integer. body-decimal = #6.4([exponent: nint, mantissa: int]) redacted_claim_keys = #7.59 redacted-element = #6.60(bstr .size 32)
; The payload: the members a family names, every text and byte member ; bounded, no free text outside body.note, absent never null. A ; member that names a row stands in `refs` and nowhere else. attestation-envelope = { ; the iss of the author: present iff the family is authored, absent ; iff counted (a column of the family model) ? "author": identity-ref, ; EVERY row this row names, by row-ref ? "refs": refs, ; the full scored dimension (leaf and :vN); it resolves to cty's ; family, refused otherwise ? "dimension": tstr, ; the blobs the row cites, by content hash: a sequence, bytes never ; hex ? "evidence_refs": [+ hash-digest], ; on the key record of a room key: the commitment the binding opens ; (seat-commitment-input) ? "seat_commitment": hash-digest, ; integers, never floats (see fixed6) ? "score": fixed6-score, ? "confidence": fixed6-unit, ? "weight": fixed6-weight, ; safety-battery interpret rows: passed <= total, both present or ; both absent, with ? "passed": count32, ; score = round(10^6 * (2*passed - total) / total), ties away from ; zero, checked by exact equality ? "total": 1..4294967295, "asserted_at": ms-time, ? "valid_from": ms-time, ? "valid_until": ms-time, ? "expires_at": ms-time, ; a code from a closed registry, 0 = unspecified ? "reason": uint, ; required where the content is low-entropy (a ballot, a census ; cell); bound by every signer ? "salt": bstr .size 16, ; on a counted row that ends a standing: only the count's own ; receipts keep an act in force ? "lifts": true, ; on an offer: whose receipts keep in force the acts exercised ; under it ? "receipter": identity-ref, ; SD-CWT simple(59): digests of the blinded members, in mint order ; (a sequence) ? redacted_claim_keys => [+ bstr .size 32], ? "body": body, ; the members a family names, under the logical names of the CC ; 2.6.1 table * tstr => ceg-value, }
body = { ? "note": tstr .size (0..2048), ? redacted_claim_keys => [+ bstr .size 32], * tstr => ceg-value } count32 = 0..4294967295
; Erasability: the selective disclosure of ; draft-ietf-spice-sd-cwt-09. A blinded map member is absent from its ; map, and the digest of its disclosure stands in that map's ; simple(59) array; a blinded array element is tag 60 over that ; digest. The digest is SHA-256 (no sd_alg) over the disclosure's ; bytes as sd_claims carries them. A family whose erasure_route is ; dsar or purge mints every free-text member and every member another ; party authored blind, body.note first; the members are the family ; model's `blind` column, and no fold, verdict or admission reads ; one. sd-disclosure = salted-claim / salted-element salted-claim = [salt: bstr .size 16, value: ceg-value, key: tstr] salted-element = [salt: bstr .size 16, value: ceg-value] ; What a blinded element of a leaf vouch discloses (CC 5.1): the ; `value` of its salted-element. The leaf's Ed25519 public key, the ; room it is vouched for, and the suite, the constant 0x004D. leaf-vouch-entry = [leaf_key: bstr .size 32, room: group-ref, suite: 77] ; POSIX milliseconds, no tag, never a float ms-time = uint
; Integers at one fixed scale: fixed6 is the value times 10^6. Folds ; sum in checked i64 and refuse on overflow, never wrap. A derived ; value is rounded ties away from zero, in integers, unless its own ; rule states otherwise, and checked by exact equality. The default ; ranges are these; weight is [0, 10^6] by rule, and a family that ; states a wider range for it states it in its own rule. fixed6 = -9223372036854775808..9223372036854775807 fixed6-score = -1000000..1000000 fixed6-unit = 0..1000000 fixed6-weight = fixed6
; The row id: the digest a row is NAMED by. One per row, the same for ; every voice of a counted row, unchanged when a voice, a receipt or ; a disclosure is added. Signatures, kid, alg, receipts and ; disclosures are outside it. `type` and `family` are the header's ; -70001 and -70002; `sub` is the CWT sub; `author` is the payload's ; "author" for an authored family and null for a counted one; ; `payload` is the payload bstr as signed, entered as a byte string, ; never as the decoded map. A payload whose bytes are not the ; deterministic re-encoding of the value they decode to is refused, ; so one row has one payload and one id. row-id-input = ["CEG-row/2", type: row-type, family: family-id, sub: tstr, author: identity-ref / null, payload: bstr .cbor attestation-envelope] row-id = hash-digest
; SHA-256 only in this edition: one name per row hash-digest = [ alg: -16, digest: bstr .size 32 ]
; A reference to a signed object of this form: the row id above, or ; the object id (below) of a signed object that is not a row. No row ; of this form names an object of the earlier form (CC 8.11, CC ; 2.6.1.12), so the edition is the constant 2. Never an ; attestation_id. row-ref = [ edition: 2, id: hash-digest ] ; a set: sorted by the bytewise order of each element's encoding, no ; duplicate row-ref-set = [+ row-ref]
; Every member that names a row. A verifier gathers the named set ; from `refs` alone, without knowing the family. SET RULE: every ; array inside `refs` is a set: its elements sorted by the bytewise ; order of each element's deterministic encoding, no duplicate, ; refused otherwise. An empty `refs` is refused: absence is its one ; encoding. refs = refs-members .and nonempty-map refs-members = { ; the roster head this row is counted over, or a version extends; ; the head an act is exercised at; the head an end acts from ? "head": row-ref, ? "further_heads": row-ref-set, ; further tips named beside `head` ; the predecessor in a signer's own series; on a content row, a ; content row its author signed in the same room ? "prev": row-ref, ; on a content row: further content rows of the same author in the ; same room, beside `prev` (CC 3.1.3.2) ? "further_prev": row-ref-set, ; the proposal voted on or accepted, the window opened, the row ; replied to ? "answers": row-ref, ; the row superseded, withdrawn, recanted, cut or removed ? "target": row-ref, ; on a key revocation: the last rows of the revoked key held good; ; on a row that ends a member's seat and on a keeps row: the ; member's newest content rows held good; at most 64 ? "trusted_through": row-ref-set, ; any other named row, under a role of the closed registry ? "also": { + also-role => row-ref-set }, } ; The also roles, closed: "ack" names a row acknowledged (a ; revocation snapshot's scope head, the acts a receipt acknowledges); ; "cites" names the row a row cites, as a build attestation names its ; manifest contribution; "under" names the one row a deputy's edge ; hangs from, a set of exactly one; "stands_on" names the one ; acceptance a row signed under a root grant stands on, a set of ; exactly one; "voice" names the head of the key roster of the voice ; a room key signs for, a set of exactly one (CC 2.6.1.11). Any other ; role is a later registration. also-role = "ack" / "cites" / "under" / "stands_on" / "voice" nonempty-map = { + any => any }
; The CEG statement id (a name of this profile; RFC 9943 defines no ; statement identifier): SHA-256 over the deterministic encoding of ; this labelled structure. It names a statement, one voice; the row ; id names the row. statement-id-input = ["CEG-statement-id/2", protected: bstr, payload: bstr] statement-id = hash-digest
; The second consent. A statement over an authored payload whose iss ; is not the payload's "author" is accepted only in a role the family ; names (delegate, bound node, ...), and only when its iss is the ; party that role names in the payload, or the CWT sub where the role ; is the attested key; any other iss is Invalid. The second consent ; of a scoped delegates_to is such a statement, by the delegate (the ; sub), over the same payload bytes, and so has the same row id; a ; scoped delegation of this form seats only with it. second-consent = ceg-statement
; Keys: one AKP COSE_Key (RFC 9964 kty 7) whose alg is the composite ; and whose pub is the composite public key encoding of the pinned ; draft revision: the ML-DSA-65 public key (1952 bytes) then the ; Ed25519 public key (32 bytes). The kid is its RFC 9679 thumbprint, ; computed under the private-use alg and fixed for the key's life. A ; composite key never verifies on one half. ceg-key = { 1: 7, 3: composite-alg, -1: bstr .size 1984 }
; A key record is a ROW on family key:record (CC 2.4.1.1 renews it by ; supersedes and rotates it by naming it), so these are members of ; its attestation-envelope, not a separate typ. identity_type is a ; SET of roles (CC 4.5.8). The end rule reads "contains", in prose ; (CC 2.4.1.1): a set mixing user or accord_holder with node or agent ; is refused; a record whose set contains user or accord_holder ; carries no valid_until; one whose set contains node or agent ; carries one, unless it is a room key, a record that carries `room`; ; a role outside both groups takes no end rule of its own; ; asserted_at < valid_until <= asserted_at + key_record_max_secs * ; 1000; refused key_record_out_of_window otherwise. key-record-members = { "key": ceg-key, "identity_type": [+ tstr], ; a set "asserted_at": ms-time, ? "valid_until": ms-time, ; iff the key is a room key: the one room it is made for (CC ; 3.1.3.2); the end rule reads it ? "room": group-ref, ; iff the key is a room key: its X-Wing KEM key, the target of ; every wrap to it ? "kem_xwing_pubkey": bstr .size 1216, ; iff the key is a room key: this record is the key's seat row ? "seat_commitment": hash-digest, ? "attestation_evidence": attestation-evidence, * tstr => ceg-value, } ; The custody of the key's Ed25519 half (CC 4.2.2, CC 4.2.2.1). ; `chain` is X.509 DER, leaf first: a sequence, required where the ; class's mechanism has a chain (Apple_Secure_Enclave, ; YubiKey_5_FIPS, TPM_2_0), refused ; key_record_bad_attestation_evidence otherwise. Where a holder is ; seated, the reader verifies it to the mechanism's attestation root ; and binds the attested key to the record's Ed25519 half. attestation-evidence = { "hardware_class": tstr, ? "pq_custody": "same_element" / "removable_offline" / "software_wrapped", ? "chain": [+ bstr], }
; A recovery commitment (CC 3.2 T3, CC 4.2.6): [-16, SHA-256 over the ; deterministic encoding of this array]. `keys` is a set of composite ; keys, sorted by encoding; a holder's recovery commitment has one ; element. recovery-commitment-input = ["CEG-recovery/2", keys: [+ ceg-key]]
; The signed objects that are not rows, each its own typ, closed: a ; verifier refuses any other typ. No cty; the payload is .cbor the ; rule its typ names, in the deterministic encoding. ceg-object-statement = #6.18([ protected: bstr .cbor object-protected, unprotected: unprotected-header, payload: bstr, signature: composite-signature, ]) object-protected = { 1: composite-alg, 4: kid, 15: object-claims, 16: object-typ, } object-claims = { 1: identity-ref, ; iss ; iat where the object states an instant; a revocation snapshot ; carries none, a genesis bundle floor(asserted_at / 1000) ? 6: uint, -70003: 2, } object-typ = "ceg-genesis-bundle/2" / "ceg-revocation-snapshot/2" / "ceg-boot-manifest/2" ; The payload rule of ceg-boot-manifest/2 waits on its owner's ; submission; no rule here stands in for it. ceg-typ = "ceg-row/2" / object-typ
; A signed object that is not a row is named like a row, so prev and ; every row-ref to it have a defined id: SHA-256 over the ; deterministic encoding of this array, written as a hash-digest. The ; domain label keeps it apart from a row id; like the row id it is ; the same for every voice of a counted object (a genesis bundle). ; `author` is the payload's "author", or null where it has none. object-id-input = ["CEG-object/2", typ: object-typ, author: identity-ref / null, payload: bstr]
; A revocation snapshot (typ "ceg-revocation-snapshot/2"): a signer's ; own record of the revocations whose past it holds. A set with no ; winner across signers. `seq` orders one signer's own snapshots: ; strictly greater than prev's, refused otherwise; two snapshots of ; one signer with one seq and different content are contested, and ; neither counts. refs carries prev (absent on the first) and, under ; also "ack", the signer's acknowledgement of the head of the ; revocation scope. Its named set is refs with each revoked entry's ; revocation and trusted_through. revocation-snapshot = { ; the signer, so the object id, prev and seq are one signer's "author": identity-ref, "refs": refs, "seq": uint, "revoked": [* revoked-entry], ; a set } ; a tuple; its trusted_through a set revoked-entry = [key: kid, revocation: row-ref, trusted_through: [* row-ref]]
; The genesis bundle (typ "ceg-genesis-bundle/2"), the GenesisBundle ; of CC 5.3.4. The first of this form is the ceremony row of CC ; 2.6.1.12: a fresh genesis with no prev, a signed object that is not ; a row. refs.prev names a later bundle's predecessor. `version` is a ; sequence from 1, never ranked: prev's version + 1 where the bundle ; has a prev, a consistency check only. A counted object: one ; statement per holder over one payload, with no "author", so its ; object id takes null. The map is closed. It NAMES rows and never ; copies them: every row it seats stands in refs.also "cites" by ; row-ref (each holder's and each seat's key:record, each seat's ; transport_destination binding). The bundle's own count is the ; canonical conferral of every seat in serve_nodes (CC 4.2.1); each ; statement carries iat, floor(asserted_at / 1000). A recovery (CC ; 2.6.1.11) is a later bundle with ONE statement: iss the holder's ; identity reference, kid the recovery key's thumbprint; it counts ; only where prev's recovery_commitments[iss] equals the commitment ; over the recovery key (constant time). refs.also "cites" names the ; recovery key's key:record and the holder's new signing-key record; ; recovery_commitments[iss] is the next commitment. Checked in prose, ; not here: version is 1 iff refs has no prev; holders, serve_nodes ; and transparency_services are pairwise disjoint; the keys of ; recovery_commitments are exactly holders; scope holds infra:attest ; and infra:serve; the three transparency members are present ; together or not at all, and receipt_quorum is ; floor(|transparency_services| / 2) + 1; each statement's iat is ; floor(asserted_at / 1000). ceg-genesis-bundle = { "refs": genesis-refs, "version": 1..4294967295, "asserted_at": ms-time, ; the accord's name, as its rows carry it; a name, never an anchor ; (CC 5.3.4) "family_key_id": tstr, ; a set: the accord's roster, the voices this bundle seats "holders": [+ identity-ref], "serve_nodes": [+ identity-ref], ; a set: the seated serve nodes "charter": genesis-charter, } genesis-refs = { ; the predecessor bundle's object id; absent on the first ? "prev": row-ref, ; every row the bundle names: a set "also": { "cites": row-ref-set }, } ; The accord's charter (CC 2.1, CC 3.2 T3 and T6, CC 4.2.6): the ; parameters no row carries. genesis-charter = { ; one entry per holder, keyed by its identity-ref "recovery_commitments": { + identity-ref => hash-digest }, ; a set; holds infra:attest and infra:serve (CC 3.2 Rooted) "scope": [+ tstr], ; absent means 86400 (CC 4.2.1.1) ? "halt_fuse_secs": 1..4294967295, ; absent: attachable by an out-of-band anchor only (CC 3.2 T4a) ? "attach_window_secs": 1..4294967295, ; where the charter names services: the three transparency members ; together ? "receipt_cadence_secs": 1..4294967295, ; absent where the charter names no services; 0 is never written ? "receipt_quorum": 2..4294967295, ; a set; each one's key:record stands in refs.also "cites" ? "transparency_services": [+ identity-ref], }
; The accord's rows (CC 4.2.1.1, CC 4.2.1.3): payloads of ordinary ; rows, so these are members of their attestation-envelope, as a key ; record's are. An invocation (the families ; accord:invoke:constitutional, accord:invoke:notify and ; accord:invoke:drill, each over its id) is ONE holder's statement ; over this payload, verified against the holders of the bundle in ; force. There is no inner signature and no text preimage; the row's ; type and family separate the kinds, so the payload carries no ; invocation_kind. The map is closed. The row is a claim, type ; scores; its sub is the accord's family_key_id (the value of ; accord_root). valid_until is later than asserted_at, refused ; valid_until_not_after_asserted_at otherwise (checked in prose). accord-invocation = { ; the holder who signs: the statement's iss "author": identity-ref, ; the accord's family_key_id: picks the bundle in force the row is ; verified against "accord_root": tstr, ; the id of the halt, the notify or the drill "invocation_id": tstr, ; minted by the holder; single-use within valid_until "nonce": bstr .size 32, "asserted_at": ms-time, ; bounds the reuse of the nonce, never the reach of a halt "valid_until": ms-time, ; a notify only: SHA-256 over its message, a separate object held ; as bytes ? "payload_digest": hash-digest, } ; A lifecycle row (family accord:lifecycle, over its kind) is counted ; (CC 2.6.1.9): one statement per holder over one payload, with no ; author. Its dimension names its kind, confirmed or active; ; refs.target names the halt it confirms or ends, and refs.head the ; bundle it is counted over. The map is closed. accord-lifecycle = { "refs": accord-lifecycle-refs, "dimension": tstr, "accord_root": tstr, "invocation_id": tstr, "nonce": bstr .size 32, "asserted_at": ms-time, "valid_until": ms-time, } accord-lifecycle-refs = { ; the bundle in force the row is counted over, by its object id "head": row-ref, "target": row-ref, ; the halt row it confirms or ends }
; The transport destination binding (CC 3.3.6.2): the payload of an ; identity:occurrence row, authored and signed by the identity it ; binds. The two X-Wing keys stand at the payload's top level, beside ; the transport_destination map; a seat's binding names its own key ; record in refs under also "cites". transport-destination-binding = { "transport_destination": transport-destination, ; on a node that relays, and on every seat ? "transit_xwing_pubkey": bstr .size 1216, ; on a node that relays, and on every serve node ? "onion_hop_xwing_pubkey": bstr .size 1216, ; on a node that opts out of relaying, with no hop key ? "onion_relay": { "opt_out": true }, ; places to dial, most preferred first: each a type and a body, the ; body that of the node code (CC 2.6.8) ? "dial_hints": [1*8 [uint .le 255, bstr .size (0..255)]], ; on a seat's binding: its key record under also "cites" ? "refs": refs, ; the content-KEM keys of CC 3.3.6.1 where they ride this row * tstr => ceg-value, } ; The RNS members of CC 3.3.6.3; destination_hash is recomputed from ; the other four. transport-destination = { "reticulum_x25519_pubkey": bstr .size 32, "reticulum_ed25519_pubkey": bstr .size 32, "app_name": tstr, ; a sequence: the hash reads the aspects in this order "aspects": [* tstr], "destination_hash": bstr .size 16, }
; Room keys. The seat commitment of a private room: SHA-256 over the ; deterministic encoding of this array, carried as "seat_commitment" ; on the room key's own key record, which is its seat row, and opened ; by the binding. `room` is the room's derived id, the `room` of that ; record. `nonce` is 32 fresh random bytes. The binding key of an ; identity is the member room_binding_xwing_pubkey of its ; identity:occurrence; its halves and those of the other KEM keys on ; that row are distinct bytes, refused at admission otherwise. seat-commitment-input = ["CEG-seat/2", room: group-ref, room_key: kid, person: identity-ref, nonce: bstr .size 32]
; A group's id (a family's, a community's, an affiliation's) is ; derived from its first version and chosen by nobody: "group-" ; followed by the base64url, without padding, of SHA-256 over the ; deterministic encoding of group-id-input. `first_members` is the ; key of every member the first version lists, a set. The form tells ; a group from a key: a key's identity reference is a thumbprint URI, ; and a group's id is never one. group-ref = tstr .regexp "group-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{42}[AEIMQUYcgkosw048]" group-id-input = ["CEG-group/2", group_kind: "family" / "community", first_members: [+ identity-ref], founded_at: ms-time, nonce: bstr .size 32] ; The binding of a voice to its person (CC 2.6.1.11, CC 3.1.3.2): a ; claim, a challenge and a confirmation. The challenge is an X-Wing ; encapsulation to the person's binding key (1120 bytes). The ; confirmation is an RFC 9180 HPKE seal in mode_psk (KEM 0x647a, ; HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM) to the addressee's room key's ; kem_xwing_pubkey, with psk the challenge's shared secret, psk_id ; SHA-256 over the challenge, info the deterministic encoding of ; binding-info-input, empty aad and plaintext the deterministic ; encoding of binding-opening. No MAC and no seed. `binding_key` is ; the thumbprint of the person's binding key; its encoding waits on ; its owner's submission. binding-info-input = ["CEG-binding/2", room: group-ref, room_key: kid, addressee_key: kid, seat_commitment: hash-digest, binding_key: bstr .size 32] binding-opening = [person: identity-ref, nonce: bstr .size 32] ; What a wrap to a room key seals, and what a sealed envelope to one ; room key carries outside a wrap: the plaintext of an HPKE mode_base ; seal under the same three identifiers. A wrap carries `dek`; an ; envelope carries none. Each flow of a binding rides here and never ; as a cleartext member of a row. room-sealed = { ; on a wrap to a room key: the wrapped key ? "dek": bstr .size 32, ; from the room key's holder: the person it names ? "claim": binding-claim, ; from the addressee: the encapsulation to the person's binding key ? "challenge": bstr .size 1120, ; from the room key's holder: the seal the addressee opens ? "confirmation": binding-confirmation, } binding-claim = { "person": identity-ref, ; the statements of the person's identity:occurrence row that ; carries the binding key ? "occurrence": [+ bstr], } binding-confirmation = { ; the confirmation's own X-Wing encapsulation "enc": bstr .size 1120, ; the AEAD ciphertext over binding-opening "ct": bstr, } ; A room's MLS group ids (CC 5.1): each is SHA-256 over the ; deterministic encoding of its array, so a door recomputes which ; room a group is of. `call` is the call's id; the member that ; carries it waits on its owner's submission. mls-group-id-input = ["CEG-mls-group/2", room: group-ref] mls-call-group-id-input = ["CEG-mls-call-group/2", room: group-ref, call: bstr] ; The HPKE info of an invitation and of a wrap to a room key, as ; text. A confirmation's info is binding-info-input. The bytes of ; each are fixed with the verifier's known-answer vectors, not in ; this file. hpke-info = "CEG-invitation/2" / "CEG-room-wrap/2"
; Verification has three answers, returned by a verifier and never on ; the wire: Valid; Invalid(reason); Waiting{missing key refs}. ; Invalid under a held key is final. A structural fault is Invalid ; whatever keys are held. A statement whose key record is Waiting is ; Waiting, naming the deepest missing key; a key record Invalid makes ; the statement Invalid. A key is one composite key: a statement ; whose signer's key record is not held is Waiting on it. Waiting is ; never counted.
; Receipts are COSE Receipts (RFC 9942) with vds = 1 ; (RFC9162_SHA256); each Transparency Service registers a statement ; in its own log and issues its own receipt over that log's root, ; with its instant of issue; a receipt is issued per batch of a ; stream, never per chunk.

section.name: Test Vectors

A key of the vectors is made from a seed n: its ML-DSA-65 seed is 32 bytes of the value n, and its Ed25519 seed is 32 bytes of the value n + 100. Both signatures are deterministic, so a second implementation that signs the same input reproduces a valid statement byte for byte.

section.name: What the Files Hold
section.t: The row statements file holds five valid statements and 50 refusals, each with its answer. It holds 17 key record payloads read alone, 6 statements read through a directory of key records, 6 statements of objects that are not rows, 11 values read as references, and 46 statements read under a family. A value read as a reference answers row for the array [-16, digest] over a 32-byte digest, key for an identity reference, and neither for anything else.

The later key-of-issuer file, key_of_iss_v3.json, holds 32 cases of steps 4, 6, 8 and 9: the end rule, a record's cover of an instant, a rotation with and without each statement, a seat in the bundle in force, an occurrence that binds a key, and a row its subject authors. In it the bound key's statement over an occurrence carries that key's own identity reference as iss. One that carries the identity's is not read as proof of possession, and the answer is Waiting on the key's statement. A key that the bundle in force seats is read from the seat, with no key record of its own. An eviction of an occurrence evicts nothing for a statement dated before the instant the eviction takes effect, and nothing at all where a key that is not of the identity signed it or where its signer's key is not held.

The earlier, key_of_iss_v1.json, holds 24 cases, and is the file with the cases of a verifier that holds bare keys, of a contested rotation, of a rival that names a record which does not cover it, and of a chain of two rotations. In both files a key record, a rotation record among them, is a scores row of the family key:record with no author. The earlier file was written before stated that a row waits for a statement it lacks, and two kinds of its answers are read by that rule today:

list.t: where a key record or a rotation record lacks a statement, the file answers invalid:kid_not_of_iss, and the answer of this document is Waiting on that statement (), as in its cases rotation_without_predecessor_statement and rotation_without_own_statement;

in two cases where the record that a rotation names is not held, rotation_genesis_not_held and rotation_two_hops_middle_missing, the file answers waiting:kid: and the key of that record, and the answer of this document is waiting:record: and that record's row id.

section.t: Every other answer of the file stands. The cases of key_of_iss_v3.json whose names begin rotation_ give the later answers.
The composer file holds 15 cases of rows read under a family: a withdraws or a recants under the family of its target, and a supersedes under its own ().

One case of the row statements file has two faults. names_earlier_form carries a faulty reference in refs.target and faulty references under refs.also, and its reason names also, which comes first in the encoding of refs.

The third version of the row statements file predates the rule that each key signs its own record, and the end rule of step 4. The fourth differs from it in three places: its directory cases are read by a key's own statement over its record (), a key record whose valid_until equals its asserted_at is refused, and the cases of a decimal fraction are added (). The other 125 cases are the same bytes with the same answers.

section.name: The Earlier Form
section.t: An earlier, retired form of the signed object was a JSON object, canonicalised with JCS and signed by a nested pair of an Ed25519 and an ML-DSA-65 signature. Revision -00 of this document described it. keeps it as an annex (CC 8.11). No node of the current edition reads it, and no row of the current form names an object of it.

section.name: Changes since draft-moore-scitt-ciris-ceg-03
section.t: Note to the RFC Editor: please remove this section before publication.

This revision brings the text to 1.0-rc22 and answers two readings of -03. One was a run of the known-answer cases from the text of -03 alone, which found five places where the text did not give the vectors' answers.
Those five:

list.t: A rotation is stated in full. A rotation record names the old key's record in refs.target, carries the new key's own statement and the old key's, keeps the old record's iss, and is made inside the old key's record. A contested rotation hands on nothing (). The table of refs says that target names the old record ().

Invalid and Waiting have one answer each. A row that is known and not held, or a statement that a held row lacks, is Waiting. Everything else is Invalid, kid_not_of_iss, and that includes a verifier that holds bare keys (). Waiting is said to name a key at step 6 and a row at step 8, in every section ().

A key's liveness at the statement's instant is read at step 6. A record covers an instant up to and not including its end, each key signs its own record, and a statement that no held record covers waits (, ). The Waiting answers are a table ().

A row type outside the five is Invalid at step 2, malformed:row-type. attestation_type_unregistered is the token a Substrate reports for the same fault. Reasons and tokens are told apart, and the three faults that have both are a table (, ).

The list of reasons gains key_record_bad_identity_type, key_record_bad_pq_custody, key_record_bad_attestation_evidence, authorship_undetermined, target_mismatch and malformed:sd-disclosure, with the Waiting answers. One rule says which member a reason names, and the prefixes of the three levels of reading are stated ().

section.name: Acknowledgments
section.t: Songbo Bu found that revision -01 did not bind a statement's signing key to the identity in iss, supplied the test cases that confirmed it, and re-ran them against the fix. The rule of is the result.

Andrii Sparysh reviewed revision -01 as an implementer would. The complete list of reasons, the pinned digests, the row id known answer, the statement of what refs.target names and of a verifier's reported state, and the log-head proposal of all follow from that review. He then ran the known-answer cases from the text of revision -03 alone, with his answers fixed before he saw the expected ones. The rotation rule of , the one answer for Invalid and for Waiting, the step at which a key's liveness is read, the two names of a row type outside the five, and the rule for naming a member in a reason are the result.

A reader of revision -03 pointed out that the statement id was named as if defined it, that the text did not say how it stands to the COSE Sig_structure, and that a match on an id could be taken for evidence of the signer. The text of and the two security considerations on the issuer and on names are the result.
The canonical-form rules in this document were found and fixed in review by the implementers of CIRISPersist, CIRISVerify and CIRISEdge.
